title: UTUVO Automix MixPlan
description: A deterministic, editable mixing plan produced from stems and a style preset.

ir_law.description: The reverb's impulse response. noise_v1 (the default, what plans without this field were rendered with) is one noise burst decaying at one rate; plate_v2 decays by band, has early reflections, builds up over 15 ms and carries nothing below 200 Hz.

timing.description: Receipt of tempo_space_v1: decay_s and pre_delay_ms were locked to the song's tempo (the beat times the power of two nearest the style's own value, within a factor sqrt(2)). The renderer reads decay_s / pre_delay_ms, not this block.

clamped.description: Which values the safety range (0.3-8 s, 5-150 ms) moved off the beat grid.

decode_policy.description: Which decoder produced the source samples. Optional: a plan without it was written before the field existed and is replayed with the legacy pcm16 decoder.

capture_groups.description: Optional receipt of the declared capture groups: which tracks are the same physical source recorded by several microphones. The renderer never reads it - the protection is already in the track numbers - and a plan without it is a normal plan.

mode.description: Only on a declared stereo pair: the two members are the declared left and the declared right channel, and they keep their own pan instead of one common pan. A group without it is the same-source group and behaves exactly as before.

trim_db.description: The shared trim of a declared stereo pair, in dB: it moves both members together.

saturation_law.description: R117: how every track's and bus's saturation (and the vocal character's) is shaped. env_tanh_os4_v1: a tanh normalised to the signal's own 30 ms peak envelope, at 4x the sample rate, RMS kept (the level contour between passages is kept; harmonics above the original Nyquist are filtered out instead of folding back). When absent: peak_tanh_v1, normalised to the single largest peak at the sample rate, as plans before R117 were rendered.

delay.description: The vocal delay that tracks' sends.delay feed. Locked to the song's tempo when it is clear (tempo records what was found), otherwise a slapback. The return is ducked while the sent signal plays and joins the fx bus.

ratio_law.description: How ratio is read. Absent means legacy_amount_v1 (plans written before this field: effective ratio 1+(r-1)^2/5 below 6). literal_v1: the ratio is the ratio.

comp_style_dial.description: R117 receipt (drum_open_v1): what the style's compression dial alone would have written into comp (ratio, attack_ms; for the drum bus also threshold_db and threshold_offset_db) before new plans opened up the drums. The renderer does not read it.

user_trim_db.description: R118: the user's group fader (vocal, drum, bass, music, fx), in dB, applied after every automatic balance; the group's reverb and delay returns move with it (fx: the returns bus itself). Absent: 0 dB, as plans before R118 were rendered.

comp_style_dial.description: R117 receipt (drum_open_v1): what the style's compression dial alone would have written into comp (ratio, attack_ms; for the drum bus also threshold_db and threshold_offset_db) before new plans opened up the drums. The renderer does not read it.

balance.description: After bus processing the renderer measures a bus where it plays (median of 3 s K-weighted windows) and moves the whole bus to target_db, within the limits: the vocal bus (vocal_var_v1) against everything else, the drum and bass buses (part_var_v1) against the rest of the band without the vocal; drums and bass first, then the vocal. Plans without it are rendered as before.

max_boost_db.description: Largest boost. When absent: 9 dB for vocal_var_v1, 6 dB for part_var_v1 (planners always write it).

max_cut_db.description: Largest cut. When absent: 6 dB for both laws (planners always write it; part_var_v1 plans from R116 on write 12 dB).

style_db.description: What the style alone asks for: for the vocal, the professional median plus the style's vocal_forward_db and techniques.vocal_lift_db.

source_db.description: The vocal against the rest in the stems as delivered; only recorded when their balance was vouched for.

meter.description: How the balance is measured. master_eq_v1: through the master EQ (what the listener hears). When absent: the buses as they are, as plans before R116 were rendered.

sends.description: R117: what happens to the reverb and delay sends of this bus's tracks when the balance moves the bus. post_fader_v1: their returns follow it (scaled by the same gain, as a post-fader send on a console). When absent: only the dry bus moves and the returns stay where they were, as plans before R117 were rendered.

duck.description: Bass bus only: a sidechain. The bass bus dips by up to depth_db while the key tracks (the kick, or a whole kit's low end) hit; the dip follows how hard they hit. Plans without it are rendered as before.

parallel.description: Drum bus only: New-York compression. A hard-compressed copy is mixed under the bus at blend of its level and the sum is returned at the bus's own level. Plans without it are rendered as before.

character.description: Vocal bus only: weight and edge after the bus compressor -- a parallel compressed copy (parallel_blend of the bus level, sum returned at the bus level), saturation, then body (220 Hz), presence (4 kHz) and air (11 kHz shelf) EQ. The vocal balance step that follows sets the level. Plans without it are rendered as before.

max_gr_p95_db.description: Squash guard: when the loudest 5% of the song (50 ms windows) loses more than this to the limiter, the master gives back loudness instead (at most max_backoff_db). Plans without it are rendered as before.

law.description: How the true-peak limiter moves its gain. tp_fast_v1 (the default, what plans without this field were rendered with) lets go of a peak within about 2 ms; tp_release_v1 ramps in ahead of a peak at 1 dB/ms and releases at 30 dB/s, like a mastering limiter, without the audio-rate gain flutter that sounds clipped.

side_air_db.description: A high shelf above 5 kHz on the side signal only: a wider top end; the mono fold-down (the mid) is unchanged. Plans without it are rendered as before.
